# @mozaik-ai/cloud-sdk

Send events to [mozaik cloud](https://app.jigjoy.ai) from any Node app — no Mozaik runtime required. Running a Mozaik runtime? Import the exporter from `@mozaik-ai/cloud-sdk/exporter` — a Participant that joins the bus and forwards everything automatically (`@mozaik-ai/core` is an optional peer, needed only for that entrypoint).

## Setup

Put your credentials in the environment or a `.env` file in the working directory:

```
MOZAIK_API_KEY=pk_...
MOZAIK_PROJECT_ID=prj_...
```

`MOZAIK_API_KEY` authenticates (the server derives the project from it); `MOZAIK_PROJECT_ID` is the project's handle shown in the UI — informational for now. Both are shown on first sign-in at https://app.jigjoy.ai. `MOZAIK_PROJECT_KEY` is accepted as a legacy alias for the key. No key found? The client never throws — it logs one warning and returns a disabled no-op client (`enabled: false`), so instrumented apps run unchanged without credentials. Optional overrides: `MOZAIK_CLOUD_ENDPOINT` (default `https://api.app.jigjoy.ai`), `MOZAIK_CLOUD_APP_URL`.

## Pairing — no key copying

```bash
npx @mozaik-ai/cloud-sdk pair
```

Prints a short code and an approve link; open it in the browser where you're signed in to app.jigjoy.ai, click **Approve device**, and the key lands in `~/.mozaik/credentials.json` (0600). From then on `createCloudClient()` finds it on its own — no `.env` needed. First-time users get their project created by the same click. Programmatic: `await pairDevice()` from the package does the same.

Credential resolution order: `projectKey` option → `MOZAIK_API_KEY` → `MOZAIK_PROJECT_KEY` (legacy) → paired credentials for the endpoint.

## Usage

```ts
import { createCloudClient } from "@mozaik-ai/cloud-sdk"

const client = createCloudClient() // prints ▶ watching live: https://app.jigjoy.ai/?s=<sessionId>

client.send({ type: "inference.started", producerId: "planner", payload: { model: "glm-5.2" } })
client.send({ type: "inference.completed", producerId: "planner", payload: { answer: "..." } })

await client.end() // flushes and closes the session
```

- `send({ type, payload, producerId?, occurredAt? })` — batched (100 events or 1s, whichever first). Unknown producers are auto-announced as agents; call `client.join({ id, name, role })` first if you want a different name/role in the roster.
- Event types the loop view understands: `message_received.*`, `inference.started|stream|completed`, `function_call.started|completed`, `model.answer`. Anything else is stored and listed, just not drawn as a loop state.
- Full payloads ship by default. For privacy set `MOZAIK_REDACTION=content` (strips prompts/answers/tool output, keeps shape + sizes — the UI then shows `{"redacted":true,"chars":1076}`) or `all` (event types only); the `redaction` option does the same in code.
- `client.sessionUrl` is the live view; `flush()` forces a send; `stats()` shows queued/sent/dropped.

## Options

`createCloudClient({ projectKey, endpoint, sessionId, redaction, batchSize, flushIntervalMs, appUrl, envFile, onError, onSessionUrl, fetch })` — everything optional; env/.env fills the gaps. `envFile: false` disables .env reading.

## Mozaik 5: watch loops

`@mozaik-ai/core` 5 has no bus: the application drives each loop through the agent module. Wrap the module, use it as before, and every instruction that runs is reported:

```ts
import { initAgentModule, resolveAgentModule } from "@mozaik-ai/core"
import { watchLoops } from "@mozaik-ai/cloud-sdk/loops"

initAgentModule()
const agents = watchLoops(resolveAgentModule(), {
  endpoint: "https://api.app.jigjoy.ai",
  projectKey: process.env.MOZAIK_API_KEY!,
})

const agent = await agents.createAgent({ name: "assistant", instruction: "…", tools: [] })
const loop = await agents.createLoop({ agentId: agent.id, goal: "…" })
await agents.setBreakpoint({ loopId: loop.id, instruction })
await agents.advanceLoop({ loopId: loop.id }) // inference.started, then inference.completed
// ...
await agents.cloud.end()
```

An agent is announced as `participant.joined`, a new loop as `context_update.*`, an inference as `inference.started|completed` (with its token usage), a tool call as `function_call.started|completed`, and `endLoop` as `response.completed`. The provider's raw response is never sent. Batching, retries, payload caps and `MOZAIK_REDACTION` work as in the client.

## Mozaik 5: loops that survive a restart

Core keeps loops in memory, so a loop is gone when the process is. Give it this repository and every step is saved in mozaik cloud; after a restart the loop is where it stopped:

```ts
import { initAgentModule, resolveAgentModule, Loop } from "@mozaik-ai/core" // 5.0.1 or newer
import { CloudLoopRepository } from "@mozaik-ai/cloud-sdk/loop-repository"

const loops = new CloudLoopRepository({
  endpoint: "https://api.app.jigjoy.ai",
  projectKey: process.env.MOZAIK_API_KEY!,
  rehydrate: Loop.rehydrate,
})
initAgentModule({ loopRepository: loops })

// After a restart: what was left unfinished, and one of them back.
const [left] = await loops.findUnfinished()
const loop = await resolveAgentModule().getLoop(left.id)
if (loop.pendingInstruction) await resolveAgentModule().advanceLoop({ loopId: loop.id })
```

- What is kept is the loop: its goal, state, the instruction at the breakpoint and every completed one with its result. Agents and registered tools are the application's to set up again.
- An instruction that was running when the process stopped is still pending, and runs again when the loop is advanced: a tool call may happen twice.
- The provider's raw response is not sent. One instruction can be about 380 KB packed; a larger one is refused, and so is a save without a plan, trial or grant. A save that fails throws: the loop is not left unsaved quietly.
- It goes with `watchLoops`: the wrapped module saves through the same repository, so a loop is both watched and kept.

## Mozaik 4: runtime exporter

Inside a Mozaik 4 app, skip manual `send()` — join the exporter to the runtime and every bus event is forwarded automatically:

```ts
import { createCloudExporter } from "@mozaik-ai/cloud-sdk/exporter"

const cloud = createCloudExporter({
  endpoint: "https://api.app.jigjoy.ai",
  projectKey: process.env.MOZAIK_API_KEY!,
  participants: () => runtime.state.getParticipants(), // roster source
})
join(cloud.participant)
// ...
await cloud.end()
```

It synthesizes `session.started` / `participant.joined` / `session.ended`, batches, retries, caps payloads and honours `MOZAIK_REDACTION` exactly like the client. Requires `@mozaik-ai/core` 4 (optional peer — the root entrypoint never loads it); it does not load under core 5, which has no bus to join.

**One transport per runtime.** Use either the exporter (inside a Mozaik app) or `createCloudClient()` + `send()` (anywhere else), never both for the same events: each opens its own session, so every loop would arrive twice. The server folds such mirrors into one loop, but the duplicate session still costs you events.
